articles.title: Birmingham union jack art made from discarded lamp-post flags
articles.summary: The huge union jack was produced using tattered flags previously hung from lamp-posts.
articles.body:
A huge union jack artwork has been created by repurposing discarded flags from unauthorised lamp-post displays as a message of "unity".

Birmingham textile artist Clare Elisabeth said her work, titled Re-Union Jack, incorporated dozens of worn-out flags and was a response to a flag-raising movement that had "caused division in communities across the country".

The names of hundreds of notable figures from across the West Midlands have been added to the piece, with some visiting the project specifically to endorse it by adding their signature.

Elisabeth said the work, created as part of the International Day of Birmingham, celebrated the region's heritage as a "magical melting pot".

Signatories include a descendant of inventor James Watt, and members of reggae bands Steel Pulse and UB40.

The four metre by seven metre artwork was sewn and glued by a small team led by the artist, who usually works with vintage fabrics.

Unauthorised displays of union jacks and St George crosses started appearing around the country last year, including the West Midlands, with various groups behind the movement.

However, their presence in several suburbs of Birmingham led to angry clashes between opposing groups and residents who claimed their presence was divisive rather than patriotic.

Fury, threats and a film crew: How a row over flags reached boiling point

Lamp-post flags organiser has 'no regrets'

Speaking about the artwork, Elisabeth said the piece was a symbol of "togetherness".

"I thought rather than throw them away, there's got to be a way that I can repurpose them into something more positive because they have been causing a lot of division.

"We have had dozens and dozens of people join in the project so it's much more than just ours.

"It's covered in the names of influential people in the Midlands who mean a lot to people and who make the Midlands this magical melting pot that we have."

Names on it include those of Ozzy Osbourne, Duran Duran and Jorja Smith.

The artwork was shown at the city's Council House as part of International Day of Birmingham celebrations on Thursday and Friday.

articles.title: Salva pelo pai, jovem supera doença rara no fígado, vira mãe e celebra | G1
articles.standfirst: No Dia da Doação de Órgãos, conheça a história de superação da estudante Vivian Rocha Caetano, de Santa Cruz das Palmeiras (SP), que passou por transplante urgente na infância.
articles.summary: No Dia Nacional da Doação de Órgãos, conheça a história da estudante Vivian Rocha Caetano, de Santa Cruz das Palmeiras (SP), que passou por transplante urgente na infância.
articles.body:
Diagnosticada com uma doença rara no fígado logo após o nascimento, a estudante Vivian Rocha Caetano passou por um transplante urgente graças ao próprio pai, que foi o doador compatível há 18 anos.

Hoje, totalmente recuperada, a moradora de Santa Cruz das Palmeiras (SP) realizou o sonho da maternidade e celebra a vida com o pequeno Gael, de 7 meses.

Neste domingo (27), Dia Nacional da Doação de órgãos , conheça a história dessa família, que foi marcada por superação e pelo gesto de amor que uniu duas gerações.

A estudante de Santa Cruz das Palmeiras (SP) Vivian Rocha Caetano passou por transplante de fígado na infância — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

A pequena Vivian nasceu com apenas 525 gramas. A pele amarelada acendeu o alerta e o diagnóstico veio rápido: atresia de vias biliares , uma doença rara que fazia com que o fígado não funcionasse corretamente.

A única saída era um transplante urgente. "A gente começou a investigar com exame para ver o que era. Aí deu que era atresia de vias biliares, um probleminha no fígado. Ela teve que ir para São Paulo para fazer o transplante", relembrou a dona de casa Evanilda Rocha Caetano, mãe de Vivian.

Para o pai, a incerteza do momento gerava angústia constante. "Tinha medo era de perdê-la. A gente só pensava no pior", contou o motorista Luiz Carlos Caetano.

Pai de Vivian doou parte do fígado para a filha ainda bebê — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Após três meses de espera na fila, os exames confirmaram que o pai e a mãe eram compatíveis. O pai foi o doador.

"Descobrir que podia ser doador foi um alívio, porque daí não ia depender de ninguém, só da gente", destacou Luiz Carlos.

"Fomos e ficamos lá esperando. Só eu lá fora esperando os dois em cirurgia. Fiquei agoniada, demorou bastante", disse Evanilda.

Anos após a cirurgia que salvou sua vida, Vivian olha para o passado com emoção, mas enxerga o presente com gratidão. Ela cresceu, realizou o sonho de ser mãe e deu à luz o pequeno Gael, de 7 meses.

Moradora de Santa Cruz das Palmeiras, Vivian celebra a vida após transplante na infância — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

"É muita tristeza [revisitar esse passado], mas saber que estou bem já é um alívio. Graças a Deus", afirma a estudante Vivian Rocha Caetano.

O pai, que doou parte do órgão há 18 anos, agora vê a vida se renovar na figura do neto. O doador do passado hoje celebra o papel de avô de um garotão cheio de energia.

'O coração já está batendo no peito de alguém'

A história de Vivian é uma exceção em que a doação ocorreu entre vivos. Na maioria dos casos, a vida de quem espera depende da doação pós-morte e da agilidade de equipes especializadas.

A Santa Casa de São Carlos é referência na captação de órgãos e foi destaque por ter 100% de aceite das famílias entrevistadas. No ano passado, a instituição realizou 11 captações de órgãos. Neste ano, já foram registradas seis captações.

O enfermeiro Tiago Clezer da Silva, coordenador de Enfermagem da UTI, relembra o dia mais desafiador de sua trajetória, quando trabalhou quase 48 horas seguidas em duas captações simultâneas.

"É uma coisa muito gratificante saber que a gente vai salvar vida. A gente vai tirar pessoas de fila, uma pessoa que está numa máquina esperando um coração, um pulmão", relatou Tiago.

"Tivemos duas cirurgias com intervalo de duas a três horas. Como moro do lado do hospital, fui em casa rapidinho só tomar um banho, comer algo e voltar. Na hora que saí pela porta, pensei: 'Já está dando quatro horas, o coração já está batendo no peito de alguém'", completou o coordenador.

Além do trabalho de captação, o hospital busca a certificação para passar a realizar cirurgias de transplante na própria unidade.

A rotina de quem aguarda por um recomeço

Rosângela Ester Botelho Caviccioli está na espera por um transplante — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Enquanto histórias como a de Vivian inspiram, a realidade de quem continua na fila é marcada pela resiliência. No Estado de São Paulo, mais de 23 mil pessoas aguardam por um transplante.

É o caso da instrutora de autoescola Rosângela Ester Botelho Caviccioli. Há sete anos, problemas de pressão alta não controlados afetaram gravemente seus rins, exigindo uma mudança radical na rotina.

"Eu já fazia tratamento de pressão desde os meus 28 anos, que adquiri na última gravidez. A medicação já não estava sendo muito eficiente e o cardiologista percebeu que estava afetando a parte renal", explicou Rosângela.

Hoje, ela faz hemodiálise três vezes por semana, durante quatro horas por sessão, enquanto aguarda por um rim compatível.

"É complicado. Depois da hemodiálise a gente fica enfraquecida, dá tontura, a pressão cai. Até se recuperar demora um pouco. Mas estamos na fé e na esperança. Acho que é a palavra: fé e esperança", desabafou a instrutora.

No Brasil, a doação de órgãos pós-morte exige a autorização da família. Por isso, o passo principal é conversar com os parentes e expressar a vontade em vida.

Para oficializar o desejo de forma digital, é possível preencher a Autorização Eletrônica de Doação de Órgãos (AEDO) pelo site oficial . O registro é gratuito e fica disponível para consulta das equipes médicas e familiares.

articles.title: VÍDEO: incêndio atinge bar na Pampulha, em BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Ocorrência foi registrada na noite deste sábado (26). Ninguém se feriu.
articles.summary: Ocorrência foi registrada na noite deste sábado (26). Ninguém se feriu.
articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu um bar localizado na Pampulha, em Belo Horizonte, na noite deste sábado (26). Ninguém se feriu.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado por volta das 22h15. Segundo a corporação, o fogo teria começado na churrasqueira e se espalhado, atingindo principalmente o teto.

O combate às chamas durou cerca de 35 minutos e demandou cerca de mil litros de água. O local possui Auto de Vistoria do Corpo de Bombeiros (AVCB) válido.

A manicure e podóloga Angélica Vieira, que estava no bar com a família, contou que o momento foi de susto e desespero.

"Quando a gente viu aquele fogo saindo pela churrasqueira, muito fogo mesmo, a gente meio que ficou num desespero. Eu só falei: 'Gente, bora, vamos sair daqui'. A primeira coisa que eu fiz foi puxar o meu filho. [...] Quando vi, já estava realmente pegando pelo teto, mas graças a Deus todos que estavam no estabelecimento saíram, deu tempo".

A Defesa Civil de Belo Horizonte informou que não foi acionada para o endereço.

Em nota, o Bebedouro Bar & Fogo afirmou que, assim que o incêndio foi identificado, "todos os clientes e colaboradores foram evacuados em segurança".

O estabelecimento disse, ainda, que o sistema de isolamento antichamas da estrutura atuou conforme o previsto e que a unidade vai funcionar normalmente neste domingo (27).

"A segurança de nossos clientes, colaboradores e parceiros é nossa prioridade absoluta. Estamos acompanhando a situação e adotando todas as medidas necessárias para avaliar os danos e garantir a segurança das instalações", destacou a nota.

articles.title: Região de Itapetininga promove contato com a natureza através do turismo rural | G1
articles.standfirst: Propriedades oferecem lazer, contato com a natureza e experiências ligadas ao campo em Itapetininga (SP) e Angatuba (SP).
articles.summary: Propriedades oferecem lazer, contato com a natureza e experiências ligadas ao campo em Itapetininga (SP) e Angatuba (SP).
articles.body:
Região de Itapetininga promove contato com a natureza através do turismo rural — Foto: Reprodução / TV TEM

Na região de Itapetininga (SP), propriedades rurais vêm se transformando em espaços de lazer e turismo. O que antes era rotina de trabalho para os produtores agora se tornou experiência para visitantes e fonte de renda para os proprietários.

A iniciativa reúne produtores, empreendedores e profissionais do turismo, que oferecem trilhas, degustações e atividades ligadas à natureza. O objetivo é valorizar o interior e proporcionar contato direto com o campo.

Em Angatuba (SP), a produtora Bárbara Soares adaptou sua propriedade com chalés, trilhas e produção agroecológica. Ela afirma que a essência do espaço é transmitir paz e simplicidade. Com o aumento da procura, o local passou a receber turistas e ganhou estrutura para hospedagem.

A turismóloga Andressa Martins destaca que paisagens, histórias e produções locais podem se tornar atrativos. Segundo ela, cresce o interesse pelo turismo regenerativo, que envolve visitantes em ações de preservação ambiental, como o plantio de árvores e flores.

Em Itapetininga, a prefeitura organiza passeios pelos parreirais, em parceria com o Sindicato Rural e o Serviço Nacional de Aprendizagem Rural (Senar). A produção familiar de vinho virou atração turística, com degustações e visitas guiadas. O produtor Ademir Marques afirma que a interação com os visitantes ajudou a manter a vinícola ativa.

Além do vinho, o turismo rural abre espaço para conhecer bastidores da produção de queijos e outros derivados. Para a artista plástica Walkiria Paunovic, a atividade gera empregos e incentiva a profissionalização de queijarias, vinícolas e restaurantes.

A troca de experiências também beneficia os empreendedores locais, que criam parcerias e novas ideias. Para os visitantes, o turismo rural é oportunidade de relaxar e reconhecer o trabalho diário no campo.

articles.title: Filho viaja quase mil km para realizar sonho da mãe de ver Xuxa | G1
articles.standfirst: Aos 62 anos, Suely saiu de Mato Grosso do Sul rumo a Curitiba para assistir ao show da apresentadora; surpresa preparada pelo filho teve até carta como se fosse um convite da nave da Xuxa
articles.summary: Aos 62 anos, Suely saiu de Mato Grosso do Sul rumo a Curitiba para assistir ao show da apresentadora; surpresa preparada pelo filho teve até carta como se fosse um convite da nave
articles.body:
Foram cerca de 16 horas dentro de um ônibus para realizar um sonho que Suely Anderson Corrêa, de 62 anos, guarda desde a infância: ver a Xuxa de perto. Ela saiu de Campo Grande , em Mato Grosso do Sul, rumo a Curitiba, no Paraná, para assistir ao show da turnê "O Último Voo da Nave", que aconteceu neste sábado (26), na Arena da Baixada.

A viagem de Campo Grande, em Mato Grosso do Sul, até Curitiba, no Paraná, foi planejada pelo filho, Rodrigo Corrêa. Ele comprou os ingressos e preparou uma surpresa para a mãe. Para deixar o momento ainda mais especial, escreveu uma carta personalizada, como se fosse um convite oficial da "nave da Xuxa" para embarcar rumo ao show.

Quando descobriu o presente, Suely não conseguiu segurar a emoção. No vídeo gravado pelo filho, ela pula de felicidade, abraça e beija Rodrigo.

"Está mil por hora, mil por hora. Show da Xuxa", diz, enquanto tenta explicar a ansiedade para o momento.

Aos poucos, a viagem ganhou um significado ainda maior para os dois. Para Rodrigo, ter condições de levar a mãe e proporcionar a experiência que ela sempre quis é algo que não tem preço.

"Eu não estava apenas levando minha mãe a um show. Eu estava devolvendo a ela uma parte da infância, uma parte da leveza, uma parte do sonho", disse Rodrigo.

Filho transforma sonho de infância da mãe em viagem para ver Xuxa — Foto: Rodrigo Corrêa

Suely cresceu acompanhando Xuxa, cantando as músicas e assistindo aos programas que marcaram uma geração de brasileiros. Ela conta que nunca imaginou ver a apresentadora ao vivo.

"Jamais iria pensar um dia na minha vida, com 62 anos, ver a Xuxa. Uma mulher maravilhosa, fantástica", disse.

"Muito, muito, muito. Vim lá do Mato Grosso do Sul para esse melhor evento do ano que eu estou passando na minha vida", contou.

Para ela, estar ali representa muito mais do que assistir a um espetáculo.

"Tudo, amor, carinho, gratidão, tudo, tudo na vida."

A realização do sonho chega depois de anos de muita luta para Suely. Segundo o filho, ela passou por momentos difíceis, mas conseguiu recomeçar e construir uma vida mais tranquila e feliz.

Hoje, ela vive de forma simples e diz estar aproveitando as pequenas alegrias da vida.

Ao mesmo tempo em que realize o sonho de conhecer Xuxa, Suely também vive a expectativa de uma possível aposentadoria. Para ela, a conquista representa o início de uma fase de mais tranquilidade depois de tantos anos de trabalho e dificuldades.

A história ainda ganhou uma coincidência que deixou tudo mais especial.

Xuxa faz aniversário em 27 de março. Suely nasceu em 27 de abril. As duas têm o mesmo dia do mês, com apenas um mês de diferença.

Para Rodrigo, a mãe sempre foi uma "baixinha" de verdade — daquelas que cresceram acompanhando a apresentadora e que nunca deixaram o sonho de lado.

Por isso, ele não quis simplesmente entregar os ingressos. Preparou uma carta personalizada, entregou pessoalmente e registrou a reação da mãe.

Depois de cerca de 16 horas de ônibus, Suely chegou a Curitiba para realizar o sonho e foi até com a barretina, o chapéu das paquitas. A viagem de quase mil quilômetros foi feita em um ônibus semi-leito e marcou uma experiência que, segundo o filho, ficará para sempre na memória dos dois.

E Rodrigo ainda alimenta outro sonho: conseguir proporcionar à mãe alguns segundos ao lado da apresentadora, seja em um abraço ou em uma foto.

articles.title: Aprenda a fazer uma receita de bolo cremoso de jerimum com coco | G1
articles.standfirst: Receita deste domingo (27) do quadro "Bom que Só", do Inter TV Rural, o bolo tem uma consistência próxima de um pudim, com preparo simples no liquidificador.
articles.summary: Receita deste domingo (27) do quadro "Bom que Só", do Inter TV Rural, o bolo tem uma consistência próxima de um pudim, com preparo simples no liquidificador.
articles.body:
A receita deste domingo (27) do quadro "Bom que Só", do Inter TV Rural , ensina como preparar uma sobremesa prática, cremosa e com sabor marcante da culinária nordestina: o bolo cremoso de jerimum com coco.

Com uma consistência que lembra a de um pudim, o bolo combina a tradição do jerimum com a riqueza do coco fresco e o toque especial da manteiga da terra. O preparo é super simples, feito quase todo no liquidificador e utilizando poucos ingredientes.

Bolo de jerimum com coco — Foto: Divulgação

500 g de jerimum cozido em água e sal (escorrido);

200 g de açúcar (pode utilizar o demerara, se preferir);

40 ml de manteiga da terra (manteiga de garrafa);

Para untar e enfarinhar a assadeira: manteiga e farinha de trigo a gosto (ou o desmoldante de sua preferência).

No liquidificador, coloque o jerimum cozido e escorrido (pode ser com casca ou sem casca, da variedade de sua preferência, como o jerimum de leite). Adicione o açúcar, os ovos inteiros, o leite, a manteiga da terra e uma pitada de sal. Bata por cerca de 2 a 3 minutos até obter uma massa fluida e bem homogênea.

Acrescente a farinha de trigo e o amido de milho. Bata rapidamente, por cerca de 30 segundos, apenas até incorporar os ingredientes à massa.

Com o liquidificador desligado, adicione o coco fresco ralado. Misture delicadamente utilizando uma colher. A massa fica mais fluida do que a de um bolo tradicional, garantindo a textura úmida e cremosa após assar.

Despeje a massa em uma assadeira (aproximadamente 25 cm de diâmetro por 5 cm de altura) previamente untada com manteiga e enfarinhada com farinha de trigo.

Leve ao forno preaquecido entre 180 °C e 200 °C por 40 a 50 minutos, ou até que a superfície e as bordas fiquem levemente douradas. Deixe esfriar um pouco antes de servir.

Para garantir que o bolo preserve o sabor marcante do jerimum e não fique com excesso de líquido, é fundamental escorrer bem a água após o cozimento e utilizar o jerimum quando estiver bem sequinho. Isso garante uma textura macia, firme e extremamente cremosa.

articles.title: $1.04 billion Powerball winner remained anonymous for nearly a month; finally claimed the prize in Illinois
articles.summary: A $1.04 billion Powerball jackpot winner in Illinois has finally claimed the prize nearly one month after the August 12 drawing, ending the mystery over
articles.body: A $1.04 billion Powerball jackpot winner in Illinois has finally claimed the prize nearly one month after the August 12 drawing, ending the mystery over who held the winning ticket. The winner, who has chosen to remain anonymous, bought a $2 Quick Pick for a single line of Powerball numbers at Hy-Vee Fast & Fresh in Quincy. The Illinois Lottery confirmed the jackpot was the second-largest lottery prize ever won in Illinois and the eighth-largest in Powerball history. Before claiming the prize, the winner spent several weeks working with professional legal and financial advisers and chose to receive the jackpot as a lump-sum payment.Who won the $1.04 billion Powerball jackpotAccording to the Illinois Lottery, the winning ticket was a Quick Pick purchased for $2. The winner said they had bought a single line of Powerball numbers and had not imagined that the purchase would result in a $1.04 billion jackpot. “This is truly a blessing, and I’m incredibly grateful for this unexpected and extraordinary opportunity,” the winner said.The winning ticket was purchased at Hy-Vee Fast & Fresh at 310 N. 36th St. in Quincy for the August 12 Powerball drawing. The drawing's $1.04 billion jackpot ranked as the eighth-largest jackpot in Powerball history, according to the Illinois Lottery's background information.How did the winner prepare to claim the jackpotBefore claiming the prize, the winner spent several weeks working with professional legal and financial advisers. The Illinois Lottery said the winner elected to receive the prize as a lump-sum payment rather than choosing the annuity option.Amanda Crosas, manager of the Illinois Lottery Chicago Prize Centre, assisted the winner's legal representatives with the prize claim. “After eight years of processing lottery claims, I’ve had the chance to meet many winners, but a $1 billion jackpot is truly extraordinary,” Crosas said. She added that “It was exciting to see the historic prize claimed after nearly a month of anticipation.”How much did Illinois players spend on PowerballThe jackpot run began on May 4 and continued through the August 12 drawing. During that period, Illinois Lottery players purchased more than $53.8 million worth of Powerball tickets, generating $26 million for the Common School Fund, which supports K–12 public education throughout Illinois.Illinois Lottery retailers earned $2.5 million in commissions and bonuses from the jackpot run, while players purchased more than 965,000 winning Powerball tickets and collected nearly $8 million in prizes, excluding the jackpot. The retailer that sold the winning ticket, Hy-Vee Fast & Fresh, received a $500,000 retailer bonus. The winner had 12 months from the drawing date to claim the prize and 60 days from the drawing date to elect the lump-sum payment option. articles.title: 'Ma, they punched me in chest': Student's last call before death at Guwahati homestay; accused claims she 'hanged' herself
articles.summary: GUWAHATI: “Ma, they have beaten me. They punched me in the chest and assaulted me.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: “Ma, they have beaten me. They punched me in the chest and assaulted me. I am injured," these were the words 22-year-old Gauhati University student Nimisha Thakuria allegedly told her mother over the phone around 2 am on Saturday, according to her father Deep Thakuria.The family could not reach her after the call and later learnt that she had been found in a critical condition at a homestay on the outskirts of Guwahati.Nimisha was taken to Garal Primary Health Centre and later referred to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival.Police have detained her alleged companion, 26-year-old Ashiq Ali, and are investigating the circumstances surrounding her death.'Will stay at hostel with friends'Deep Thakuria said Nimisha left home around 5 pm on Friday and told her mother she might spend the night at Gauhati University hostel with friends.“She had told her mother that she would stay at Gauhati University hostel with her friends,” he said.Around 10 pm, Nimisha again told her mother that she would spend the night there.But around 2 am, she called her mother unexpectedly. “After that, we could no longer reach her. We kept calling her repeatedly, but there was no response,” Thakuria added further.The family eventually contacted Azara police station, where an officer tried to trace Nimisha's phone location.The father also told TOI, that he and his family went to Azara police station and informed the second officer-in-charge about the situation.Around half an hour later, police told the family that a girl had been found at Garal Primary Health Centre and asked them to verify whether she was Nimisha.He said police told them that if the woman was Nimisha, she would be taken immediately to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital.'She did not mention homestay'Thakuria said Nimisha had not told the family that she planned to stay at a homestay with Ashiq Ali.Instead, he said, she had told them she would be staying at the university hostel with friends. “She took Rs 2,000 just two days back, saying she would go out to eat with her friends and stay overnight at a friend's hostel,” he said.Police said Nimisha and Ashiq had been staying at a homestay in the Dharapur-Garal area. They are examining their movements and the events leading up to Nimisha being found unconscious.Police examine Ashiq's accountAshiq told police that Nimisha had hanged herself and died by suicide.Deputy commissioner of police (west) Balin Deuri said investigators would establish whether that account was true.“Whether it is true or a lie, would come out during the investigation,” Deuri said.The body has been sent for post-mortem examination, and police are awaiting the report. CID and forensic teams have also examined the homestay room and collected evidence.Homestay verification under scannerPolice said Nimisha and Ashiq had visited the homestay five times this month and were allowed to stay without proper verification.The homestay had also not collected mandatory identification documents from the two, police said. Its owner has been questioned and action will be initiated under the law.A staff member, Bipul Bailung, said Nimisha and Ashiq were staying in room number 10 and had ordered food around 9.30 pm.He claimed staff later heard shouts for help and crying in a male voice around 2.30-3 am.“Three of us went to their room and found the girl lying on the floor, with the boy holding her in his hands and crying,” Bailung said.Residents demand investigationAfter news of Nimisha's death spread, local residents blocked a road leading towards the nearby airport and staged a protest demanding a thorough investigation.Some protesters alleged that the incident was linked to what they described as “love jihad”.“We demand a proper investigation and justice so that no one involved in the incident is allowed to escape accountability. articles.title: Boeing finds software glitch that may disable landing guidance on some 737 MAX jets
articles.summary: Boeing has found a previously undisclosed software problem on some 737 MAX aircraft that could leave pilots without automated flight guidance during a
articles.body: Boeing has found a previously undisclosed software problem on some 737 MAX aircraft that could leave pilots without automated flight guidance during a particular landing situation, Wall Street Journal reported citing company documents.The problem is linked to a cockpit software update and can arise when pilots change the aircraft's planned route after a missed approach. In such a situation, an automated navigation feature may stop working during the subsequent landing attempt.Boeing said it had notified operators about the issue last month and was working on a permanent fix."We shared information with operators that reinforced existing pilot procedures for safely handling such cases. Our engineers are working on a software update to permanently address the issue," Boeing said in an emailed statement to news agency Reuters.FAA reviewing potential safety issueThe US Federal Aviation Administration said it was aware of the problem involving a software update for flight computers installed on certain 737 MAX aircraft."The FAA will convene a Corrective Action Review Board and will take immediate action if it identifies a safety concern," the agency said.The FAA, Boeing and airlines are now assessing how widely the affected software is being used and whether the problem presents a broader safety risk.Southwest Airlines and United Airlines have asked Boeing to hold back deliveries of new 737 MAX aircraft fitted with the affected software, instead requesting aircraft with an earlier software version, the Wall Street Journal reported.Latest issue adds to scrutiny of MAXIt remains unclear how many aircraft are currently operating with the software in question. The development comes as Boeing's 737 MAX programme continues to face close regulatory and safety scrutiny. The aircraft was grounded worldwide after two fatal crashes in 2018 and 2019, which together killed 346 people.Boeing also faced renewed scrutiny in January 2024 after a door plug blew out of an almost-new 737 MAX 9 operated by Alaska Airlines during a flight.The latest software issue does not mean that the aircraft is unsafe to fly. articles.title: Psychology says children behave differently with each parent for a reason; what it may reveal about their emotional comfort
articles.summary: A child who happily follows one parent’s instructions may argue with the other over the smallest things.
articles.body: A child who happily follows one parent’s instructions may argue with the other over the smallest things. They may be chatty and playful with one parent but quiet and reserved with the other. They may run to one parent after a bad day and seek the other when they want to play, explore or negotiate for something.For parents, these differences can be confusing. It can even feel unfair. “Why does our child listen to you but not me?” or “Why does she become so difficult only when I am around?” are questions many parents find themselves asking.But children are not necessarily being inconsistent- and their behaviour does not automatically mean that they love one parent more.Developmental psychology suggests that children develop individual relationships with each caregiver. Those relationships are shaped by everyday experiences: who comforts them when they are upset, who sets boundaries, who plays with them, who helps with homework, who handles bedtime and, importantly, how each parent responds when the child is overwhelmed.Research on attachment suggests that children can have different attachment relationships with different caregivers, while both relationships can contribute to emotional development and regulation.The same child can be different with different parentsAttachment is not simply something a child “has” and then carries unchanged into every relationship. It develops through repeated interactions between the child and caregiver.A study examining mother-child and father-child attachment found that relationships with mothers and fathers can have distinct patterns, while attachment to both parents can contribute to children's ability to regulate emotions.This helps explain why a child may behave differently with each parent without there necessarily being a problem.One parent may be the person associated with routines and rules. Another may be the one who spends more time playing. One may usually handle school-related responsibilities, while another may be the person who sits beside the child at bedtime and listens to their worries.Over time, children learn what to expect from each relationship.So when a child behaves differently with each parent, the more useful question may not be, “Who does my child prefer?”, but “What kind of relationship has my child developed with each of us?”Does acting out mean the child feels safer? This is where one of the most popular parenting claims needs some nuance. You may have heard that children “save their worst behaviour” for the parent they feel safest with. There is some psychological reasoning behind why a child might become more emotionally expressive around a trusted caregiver. But research does not establish that every child who tantrums, argues or becomes demanding with a particular parent is doing so because they feel safest with that parent.Children's behaviour is influenced by several factors- tiredness, hunger, overstimulation, temperament, the environment and what happened earlier in the day.The American Academy of Pediatrics notes that children may act out when they are struggling with stress or emotions they do not yet have the skills to communicate clearly.Consider a child who has spent the entire school day following instructions, managing friendships and controlling their reactions. They may appear perfectly fine at school and then burst into tears when they reach home.That does not necessarily mean they were “pretending” to be fine all day. It may simply mean that the demands of the day caught up with them.And if a particular parent has become their usual source of comfort, that is the person they may naturally seek when the emotional load becomes too much.Emotional security does not mean perfect behaviourAnother misconception is that a securely attached child should be calm, obedient and emotionally easy to handle. Attachment research paints a different picture.In practical terms, emotional security is less about whether a child throws tantrums and more about whether they have a reliable relationship in which they can seek comfort, receive support and gradually learn to manage difficult feelings.A child can therefore be securely attached and still say, “I hate you!” during a tantrum. The important part is what happens around that moment. Does the parent help the child calm down? Can they acknowledge the emotion without giving in to inappropriate behaviour? Can they reconnect after the conflict? These repeated experiences teach children that difficult emotions do not automatically threaten the relationship.Why one parent may get more tearsSometimes the difference is surprisingly ordinary. A child may become clingy when one parent returns from work because that parent has been away all day. Another child may argue more with the parent who spends the most time enforcing routines simply because there are more opportunities for conflict.A parent who handles bedtime may see more meltdowns simply because children are tired at that time of day. This is why behaviour needs to be viewed in context. Instead of concluding, “My child behaves badly with me,” parents can look for patterns: When does it happen? What happened immediately beforehand? What does the child seem to need? How does the parent respond?Those questions often reveal more than the behaviour itself.The parent's response matters tooChildren are also learning from how adults respond to emotions. If a child says, “I am scared,” and a parent immediately dismisses the feeling, the child gets a different message from one who hears, “I can see that you're scared. Tell me what happened.” This process is sometimes described as emotion socialisation- the ways parents respond to and talk about children's emotional experiences.Listening when a child talks about school. Sitting beside them after a nightmare. Helping them name anger rather than simply telling them to stop crying. Setting a boundary while still acknowledging the feeling behind the behaviour.Both parents can become a child's safe baseResearch has increasingly moved beyond the idea that attachment should be understood only through the mother-child relationship. Studies looking at both parents suggest that attachment to mothers and fathers can each contribute to children's emotional and behavioural development.That does not mean the child must behave identically with both. In fact, expecting identical behaviour may miss the point.A child may turn to one parent for reassurance and another for encouragement to explore. They may be more physically affectionate with one and more talkative with the other. These differences can exist within healthy family relationships.What matters is whether the child experiences each relationship as reasonably predictable, responsive and emotionally available.What parents should look at insteadSo, if your child behaves completely differently with you and your partner, there is no need to immediately turn it into a competition. Watch the relationship rather than the tantrum.Does your child come to you when hurt? Can they tell you when something is bothering them? Do they seek you out for reassurance? Can you set limits without making affection conditional? After an argument, can the two of you reconnect?These may tell parents considerably more about emotional comfort than whether the child is more obedient with one parent. Harvard's Center on the Developing Child describes responsive back-and-forth interactions between children and caregivers as “serve and return” - everyday exchanges that help build the foundations for social and emotional development.Ultimately, children do not need two parents who respond to them in exactly the same way. They need relationships in which they can be heard, comforted, guided and given room to grow.So the next time a child who is perfectly behaved with one parent suddenly becomes emotional, demanding or argumentative with the other, the behaviour may be worth looking at- but not necessarily as a sign of favouritism.Sometimes, it is simply a glimpse into how differently the child has learned to connect with the two people who matter most in their everyday world.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Students at Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara damaged property and blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway early Sunday
articles.body: Students at Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara damaged property and blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway early Sunday following unverified reports on social media about the alleged rape of a female student. Police said they had no information of any such crime.Police say rumours triggered campus unrestKapurthala Senior Superintendent of Police Gaurav Toora said police received information around 1.45 am that students had gathered on the LPU campus and blocked a road. Addressing the unverified rape claim, Toora said, "When we reached here, we came to know that there were rumours. Because of the rumours, students gathered here".Videos circulating on social media showed students damaging window panes and flower pots, while some objects were also seen being set on fire. The students also blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway.Students raise grievances with university administrationToora said police spoke to students who raised issues with the LPU administration and that efforts were being made to address their concerns."We spoke to students who had some issues with the LPU administration. We heard them and are trying to get them resolved. The situation is completely under control," the SSP said.He added that students told police their grievances were not being addressed properly. An assessment of the property damage is under way, and necessary legal action will be taken, Toora said.A heavy police force has been deployed at the university, with police stating that the situation is now under control.Chitkara University protest a day earlierThe incident came a day after students at Chitkara University in Patiala held a protest following unverified claims on social media that two female students had allegedly died by suicide on the campus. articles.title: AI mural inspired by Banksy sparks backlash in Bristol: Artists spot wrong landmarks and a bizarre version of the famous Mild Mild West as debate over AI art grows
articles.summary: At first glance, the huge mural on the side of a Bristol pub looks like a colourful celebration of the city.
articles.body: At first glance, the huge mural on the side of a Bristol pub looks like a colourful celebration of the city. Look a little closer, though, and the problems start to appear.The artwork was generated using AI and printed onto vinyl before being placed on the Jolly Colliers pub in Bedminster. It features Bristol landmarks, including the Cabot Tower and the SS Great Britain. It also appears to reference Banksy's famous Mild Mild West. But local artists quickly pointed out that several of those details weren't quite right.Even the Banksy reference was wrongThe most noticeable problem may be the reference to Banksy. His Mild Mild West, created in Bristol, is known for its teddy bear throwing a petrol bomb at riot police. The AI mural instead showed a strange one-legged figure pointing.Other parts of the image also raised eyebrows. Bristol24/7 reported that Cabot Tower was incorrectly depicted, while the SS Great Britain looked more like a smaller tugboat.For a city whose visual identity is so closely tied to street art, those mistakes were hard to ignore.Artists say the problem goes beyond bad detailsCaroline Maggs of the Bristol Mural Collective criticised the decision to use AI rather than commission a local artist. Speaking to Bristol24/7, she said, “AI designs not only devalue but undermine the work of artists.” She also argued that choosing AI art was not simply an aesthetic decision because artists were already facing pressure from the technology.An unsigned note was also reportedly attached to the pub, accusing those behind the mural of failing to respect Bristol's creative community. The reaction wasn't just about whether the artwork looked good. For some local artists, it was about who gets paid to make public art and whether a city famous for its artists should be using AI to imitate that culture.Why the pub says it used AIThe pub's owner, Punch Pubs, gave a different explanation. According to Bristol24/7, a spokesperson said the mural was a “temporary measure due to the condition of the external wall” and that the company planned to work with local artists and the community on a permanent mural later.So this wasn't presented as the final artwork. The company said the condition of the wall made a permanent mural difficult at the time.But that explanation didn't stop the criticism.The incident also isn't the first time artists have experimented with AI trained or designed to resemble Banksy's visual language. In 2020, The Art Newspaper reported on an AI project called GANksy, which generated images designed to resemble the anonymous British street artist's work.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘You put underdeveloped brains together’: Psychiatrist on why parents should rethink sending children away to college
articles.summary: For many parents, sending a child to college is a moment of pride.
articles.body: For many parents, sending a child to college is a moment of pride. It is also the first time they may have little idea what their son or daughter is doing after dinner, who they are spending time with or what happens behind the closed doors of a hostel room.Psychiatrist Daniel G. Amen recently raised this concern while discussing young people leaving home for college. He questioned the idea of sending young adults, whose brains are still developing, into an environment with limited adult supervision. He also pointed to the changing nature of college-party culture, where alcohol may coexist with cannabis and psychedelic substances such as psilocybin.His comments may sound alarming, but they raise a more useful parenting question: When children leave home, does parental influence really end?Research suggests it does not.The brain is still developingThe popular phrase that the brain is not fully developed until 25 is often repeated without context. Brain development is a gradual process, and areas involved in planning, decision-making, impulse control and weighing consequences continue to mature through adolescence and into young adulthood.That matters when teenagers and young adults encounter situations where immediate social rewards can compete with longer-term consequences.Cannabis, for example, is not simply a harmless substance because it is increasingly normalised in some social settings. The US National Institute on Drug Abuse notes that cannabis can affect memory, attention, learning and decision-making, with young people considered particularly vulnerable because their brains are still developing.That does not mean every young person who experiments with cannabis will develop a problem. But it does mean parents should avoid presenting it to teenagers as something with no meaningful risks.College changes the equationOne of the biggest changes after school is not necessarily college itself, but independence.A young person who previously came home to parents every evening may suddenly be making decisions about alcohol, parties, friends and sleep without anyone immediately around to intervene.Research following young people through the transition from high school to emerging adulthood has found that leaving home and entering college can coincide with increases in heavy episodic drinking. The same research also found that stronger parental monitoring during the final year of high school was associated with lower increases in heavy drinking and, among college students, fewer increases in marijuana use.This is important because monitoring does not have to mean surveillance.For an 18-year-old living away from home, it may simply mean parents continuing to know what is happening in their child's life: who their close friends are, how college is going, whether they are struggling and whether something about their behaviour has changed.The conversation should happen before the hostel roomA common mistake is to have the first serious conversation about drugs after a child has already left home. By then, the child may already have encountered situations where saying no feels socially difficult. Parents can start much earlier by talking about real situations rather than delivering a lecture.What would you do if someone handed you a drink and you did not know what was in it? What if your roommate was using cannabis? What if friends wanted you to take something before a party? What if you felt uncomfortable but were afraid of looking boring?These conversations give children something more useful than a list of forbidden substances: a script for handling pressure. It is also worth telling children that they can call home when something goes wrong without immediately fearing punishment.A young person who believes, “If I call my parents, I will be in bigger trouble,” may hesitate at precisely the moment when help is needed.Psilocybin needs a separate conversationAmen also mentioned “mushroom parties”, referring to psilocybin-containing mushrooms. The growing interest in psychedelics can make teenagers assume that because psilocybin is being studied for certain medical applications, taking it recreationally is automatically safe. That is not the same thing.The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes that research into psilocybin-assisted therapy is being conducted under controlled conditions, while also highlighting safety concerns and the importance of the mental state and physical setting in which the substance is taken.Parents therefore need to help children understand an important distinction: a substance being studied in a controlled therapeutic setting does not make unsupervised recreational use equivalent to medical treatment.Parenting does not end at 18Interestingly, research has found that parental behaviour can continue to matter even during later college years.A prospective study of 1,429 students at three US universities found associations between parental permissiveness toward alcohol and student drinking during both the first and fourth years of college. The researchers concluded that parenting remained relevant even as students moved further into adulthood.This does not mean parents can control every decision their adult children make. They cannot. The goal is different: to make sure that independence is accompanied by preparation.That preparation includes teaching children how alcohol affects judgement, discussing the risks associated with cannabis and other drugs, helping them recognise peer pressure and making sure they know when and how to seek help. It also means parents need to keep the relationship strong enough that their child can tell them the uncomfortable truth.College will inevitably bring new freedoms. Children will meet people their parents have never met and make decisions their parents cannot supervise. The most useful thing parents can give them before they leave may therefore not be another warning about parties.It may be the confidence to pause, think about the consequences, walk away when something feels wrong - and call home when they need help.You use AI every day. articles.title: Google turns 28: 10 things that Google says it first wrote when it was just few years old, and you can still hold the company to
articles.summary: Google has turned 28 today. The company still has a list of principles it says trace back to its early years.
articles.body: ​Google has turned 28 today. The company still has a list of principles it says trace back to its early years. Called “Ten things we know to be true,” the list was first written when Google was just a few years old, and the company has revisited it over time. Google says it uses the list to check whether those principles still hold true, and explicitly adds: “you can hold us to that.”From putting users first and prioritising speed to its views on advertising, access to information, work culture, and constant innovation, these 10 points show what Google said it wanted to stand for early on. Some of the principles are closely tied to its search business, while others cover broader ideas about how the company develops products and operates. Here are the 10 things Google says it first wrote down when it was still a young company.10 principles that Google wrote when it was a young companyHere are the principles that Google promised on when it was still a young company:“1. Focus on the user and all else will follow.Since the beginning, we’ve focused on providing the best user experience possible. Whether we’re designing a new internet browser or a new tweak to the look of the homepage, we take great care to ensure that they will ultimately serve you, rather than our own internal goal or bottom line. Our homepage interface is clear and simple, and pages load instantly. Placement in search results is never sold to anyone, and advertising is not only clearly marked as such, it offers relevant content and is not distracting. And when we build new tools and applications, we believe they should work so well you don’t have to consider how they might have been designed differently.2. It’s best to do one thing really, really well.We do search. With one of the world’s largest research groups focused exclusively on solving search problems, we know what we do well, and how we could do it better. Through continued iteration on difficult problems, we’ve been able to solve complex issues and provide continuous improvements to a service that already makes finding information a fast and seamless experience for millions of people. Our dedication to improving search helps us apply what we’ve learned to new products, like Gmail and Google Maps. Our hope is to bring the power of search to previously unexplored areas, and to help people access and use even more of the ever-expanding information in their lives.3. Fast is better than slow.We know your time is valuable, so when you’re seeking an answer on the web you want it right away–and we aim to please. We may be the only people in the world who can say our goal is to have people leave our website as quickly as possible. By shaving excess bits and bytes from our pages and increasing the efficiency of our serving environment, we’ve broken our own speed records many times over, so that the average response time on a search result is a fraction of a second. We keep speed in mind with each new product we release, whether it’s a mobile application or Google Chrome, a browser designed to be fast enough for the modern web. And we continue to work on making it all go even faster.4. Democracy on the web works.Google search works because it relies on the millions of individuals posting links on websites to help determine which other sites offer content of value. We assess the importance of every web page using more than 200 signals and a variety of techniques, including our patented PageRank™ algorithm, which analyzes which sites have been “voted” to be the best sources of information by other pages across the web. As the web gets bigger, this approach actually improves, as each new site is another point of information and another vote to be counted. In the same vein, we are active in open source software development, where innovation takes place through the collective effort of many programmers.5. You don’t need to be at your desk to need an answer.The world is increasingly mobile: people want access to information wherever they are, whenever they need it. We’re pioneering new technologies and offering new solutions for mobile services that help people all over the globe to do any number of tasks on their phone, from checking email and calendar events to watching videos, not to mention the several different ways to access Google search on a phone. In addition, we’re hoping to fuel greater innovation for mobile users everywhere with Android, an open source mobile platform free of charge. Android brings the openness that shaped the internet to the mobile world. Not only does Android benefit consumers, who have more choice and innovative new mobile experiences, but it opens up revenue opportunities for carriers, manufacturers and developers.6. You can make money without doing evil.Google is a business. The revenue we generate is derived from offering search technology to companies and from the sale of advertising displayed on our site and on other sites across the web. Hundreds of thousands of advertisers worldwide use Google Ads to promote their products; hundreds of thousands of publishers take advantage of our AdSense program to deliver ads relevant to their site content. To ensure that we’re ultimately serving all our users (whether they are advertisers or not), we have a set of guiding principles for our advertising programs and practices:We don’t allow ads to be displayed on our results pages unless they are relevant where they are shown. And we firmly believe that ads can provide useful information if, and only if, they are relevant to what you wish to find–so it’s possible that certain searches won’t lead to any ads at all.We believe that advertising can be effective without being flashy. We don’t accept pop–up advertising, which interferes with your ability to see the content you’ve requested. We’ve found that text ads that are relevant to the person reading them draw much higher clickthrough rates than ads appearing randomly. Any advertiser, whether small or large, can take advantage of this highly targeted medium.Advertising on Google is always clearly identified as a “Sponsored Link,” so it does not compromise the integrity of our search results. We never manipulate rankings to put our partners higher in our search results and no one can buy better PageRank. Our users trust our objectivity and no short-term gain could ever justify breaching that trust.7. There’s always more information out there.Once we’d indexed more of the HTML pages on the internet than any other search service, our engineers turned their attention to information that was not as readily accessible. Sometimes it was just a matter of integrating new databases into search, such as adding a phone number and address lookup and a business directory. Other efforts required a bit more creativity, like adding the ability to search news archives, patents, academic journals, billions of images and millions of books. And our researchers continue looking into ways to bring all the world’s information to people seeking answers.8. The need for information crosses all borders.Our company was founded in California, but our mission is to facilitate access to information for the entire world, and in every language. To that end, we have offices in more than 60 countries, maintain more than 180 internet domains, and serve more than half of our results to people living outside the United States. We offer Google’s search interface in more than 130 languages, offer people the ability to restrict results to content written in their own language, and aim to provide the rest of our applications and products in as many languages and accessible formats as possible. Using our translation tools, people can discover content written on the other side of the world in languages they don’t speak. With these tools and the help of volunteer translators, we have been able to greatly improve both the variety and quality of services we can offer in even the most far–flung corners of the globe.9. You can be serious without a suit.Our founders built Google around the idea that work should be challenging, and the challenge should be fun. We believe that great, creative things are more likely to happen with the right company culture–and that doesn’t just mean lava lamps and rubber balls. There is an emphasis on team achievements and pride in individual accomplishments that contribute to our overall success. We put great stock in our employees–energetic, passionate people from diverse backgrounds with creative approaches to work, play and life. Our atmosphere may be casual, but as new ideas emerge in a café line, at a team meeting or at the gym, they are traded, tested and put into practice with dizzying speed–and they may be the launch pad for a new project destined for worldwide use.10. Great just isn’t good enough.We see being great at something as a starting point, not an endpoint. We set ourselves goals we know we can’t reach yet, because we know that by stretching to meet them we can get further than we expected. Through innovation and iteration, we aim to take things that work well and improve upon them in unexpected ways. For example, when one of our engineers saw that search worked well for properly spelled words, he wondered about how it handled typos. That led him to create an intuitive and more helpful spell checker.Even if you don’t know exactly what you’re looking for, finding an answer on the web is our problem, not yours. We try to anticipate needs not yet articulated by our global audience, and meet them with products and services that set new standards. When we launched Gmail, it had more storage space than any email service available. In retrospect offering that seems obvious–but that’s because now we have new standards for email storage. Those are the kinds of changes we seek to make, and we’re always looking for new places where we can make a difference. Ultimately, our constant dissatisfaction with the way things are becomes the driving force behind everything we do.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bengal SIR row: CM Suvendu Adhikari pins blame on Mamata for deletion of 27 lakh voters
articles.summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari has blamed former CM Mamata Banerjee for the deletion of around 27 lakh names from the state’s electoral rolls
articles.body: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari has blamed former CM Mamata Banerjee for the deletion of around 27 lakh names from the state’s electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), rejecting allegations that the BJP or the Election Commission was responsible.Adhikari claimed the deletions were ordered by judicial officers following directions from the Supreme Court in a case filed by Banerjee herself. He accused the TMC leader of trying to shift responsibility after her defeat in the Assembly elections.“The responsibility for the deletion of 27 lakh names lies with Mamata Banerjee, not the BJP or the Election Commission. Judicial officers took the decision following the Supreme Court's directions in a case filed by her,” Adhikari said at a press conference.The Election Commission has said 22.21 lakh of the deleted voters had filed appeals seeking their names to be restored. More than 38 lakh appeals have been filed in total against both exclusions and inclusions during the SIR process.Politics over voter rollsThe SIR exercise has become a major political flashpoint in Bengal. The TMC has alleged that genuine voters were removed from the rolls and has demanded that their names be restored.Adhikari, meanwhile, sought to contrast Bengal with Kerala, where the revision exercise has also taken place.“If SIR is good in Kerala, why is it bad in West Bengal? We have won 208 seats, while the two sides (TMC and its allies) have 80. Mamata Banerjee is unable to accept the people's verdict,” he said.His comments came a day after Banerjee addressed a rally in Serampore and renewed her criticism of the Election Commission and the BJP over the voter-roll revision.Questions over election commissionAdhikari also referred to a meeting between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.He said the meeting and the poll panel’s subsequent statement showed that decisions concerning Bengal’s SIR were not taken by the CEC alone.The issue comes amid scrutiny of the functioning of the three-member Election Commission. An Indian Express investigation reported that the two election commissioners had raised objections on several occasions over decisions linked to the SIR exercise.The Election Commission has maintained that differences during internal discussions are normal and that its final decisions on the exercise were unanimous.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Central railway powers up: Freight revenue crosses rs. 3,400 crore milestone on surge in coal and automobile transit
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Central Railway (CR) on Sunday announced robust financial and operational growth, crossing the Rs 3,400 crore mark in freight revenue during the
articles.body: MUMBAI: Central Railway (CR) on Sunday announced robust financial and operational growth, crossing the Rs 3,400 crore mark in freight revenue during the first five months of the current financial year. Driven by strong industrial demand and a surge in August performance, the network continues to play a vital role in the national supply chain.Between April and August 2026, CR transported 34.48 million tonnes (MT) of freight across 13,058 rakes, marking a 7% increase in tonnage compared with the 32.10 MT moved during the same period last year. Total freight earnings reached Rs 3,461.92 crore, up from Rs 3,346.80 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.Automobile traffic also saw a notable increase, rising to 451 rakes from 357 rakes in the previous year — an addition of 94 rakes.Industrial hubs played a leading role in driving these numbers, with the Nagpur and Mumbai divisions accounting for the largest shares of both tonnage and revenue. The Nagpur Division contributed 20.31 MT, representing a 58.90% share, and generated Rs 2,072.73 crore, accounting for 59.87% of total revenue. The Mumbai Division followed with 8.56 MT, a 24.83% share, generating Rs 800.49 crore, or 23.12% of total revenue.Bulk commodities continued to form the backbone of CR's freight basket, led by coal and containers. Coal remained the top commodity, with 17.00 MT transported across 4,291 rakes, generating Rs 1,556.87 crore. Containers were second, with 4.33 MT transported across 3,958 rakes, generating Rs 413.43 crore.Petroleum products and cement also recorded steady movement, at 2.91 MT and 2.82 MT respectively. Other essential commodities, including iron ore, fertilisers, food grains, sugar and onions, also contributed to the diversified logistics mix.August proved to be a milestone month, with CR recording its highest freight loading for August in the last 10 years at 6.85 MT. Monthly tonnage rose 22% across 2,567 rakes compared with August 2025, while revenue increased by more than 17% to Rs 684.78 crore.With targeted infrastructure enhancements, expanded terminal capacities and customer-focused logistics solutions, Central Railway remains positioned to support efficient freight movement and broader economic activity.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Switzerland's neutrality test puts Nato ties, Russia sanctions at stake
articles.summary: Swiss voters are deciding on Sunday whether to tighten the country's neutrality rules, in a referendum that could restrict its peacetime military
articles.body: Swiss voters are deciding on Sunday whether to tighten the country's neutrality rules, in a referendum that could restrict its peacetime military cooperation with Nato and limit its ability to impose sanctions on countries involved in wars.According to Reuters, the proposed constitutional amendment would prevent Switzerland from cooperating with military or defence alliances during peacetime, unless the country itself were attacked or an attack were imminent. It would also restrict Switzerland from joining sanctions against countries involved in conflicts, with exceptions including measures mandated by the United Nations.Switzerland is not a Nato member, but it has maintained cooperation with the alliance for decades while retaining its neutral status. Nato says Switzerland joined the Partnership for Peace programme in 1996 and cooperates with the alliance on areas including military interoperability, defence capabilities and peace-support activities.The proposed changes could therefore affect existing forms of Swiss-Nato cooperation. Reuters reported that Swiss foreign minister Ignazio Cassis has warned that the initiative could prevent Switzerland from training with Nato and reduce its ability to prepare for potential security crises.Russia sanctions at the centre of debateThe referendum also puts Switzerland's policy towards Russia under scrutiny. Bern adopted sanctions against Moscow following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, largely aligning itself with measures imposed by the European Union.Supporters of the initiative, led by the right-wing Swiss People's Party, argue that such measures have compromised Switzerland's neutrality. Christoph Blocher, a prominent backer of the proposal, told Reuters that Russia now considers Switzerland a party to the conflict because of its sanctions.The initiative would establish a stricter framework under which Switzerland could generally not participate in sanctions unless they were imposed by the United Nations or fell under specified exceptions.Government warns against isolationThe Swiss government opposes the proposal, arguing that neutrality does not mean isolation.Bern says Switzerland can remain neutral while cooperating with other countries to strengthen its security. The government has also argued that military cooperation and interoperability need to be developed during peacetime rather than only after a conflict begins.The debate has gained significance as European countries strengthen their defence capabilities amid the continuing Russia-Ukraine war.The referendum is therefore not about whether Switzerland will remain neutral. Instead, it is about how strictly that neutrality should be applied and whether it should limit Switzerland's military and diplomatic cooperation with other European countries.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1873, Andrew Hallidie tested San Francisco’s first cable car on Clay Street, creating a new way to travel up the city’s steep hills without horses
articles.summary: In August 1873, San Francisco tested a new cable railway system designed to operate on streets where horses struggled with steep grades.
articles.body: In August 1873, San Francisco tested a new cable railway system designed to operate on streets where horses struggled with steep grades. Andrew Smith Hallidie tested the first cable car on Clay Street on 2 August, using an endless wire rope placed in a tube below the surface of the street. The Clay Street Hill Railroad began public service on 1 September 1873. Its route climbed a hill rising 307 feet above Kearny Street, with the steepest grade recorded as 1 in 6 15/100. The cable system later spread across San Francisco, while cable cars continued serving steep hills as electric streetcars and buses expanded.How the San Francisco cable car climbed steep hills without horsesAccording to the Cable Car Heritage Museum, a contemporary description by A. S. Hallidie, reproduced by the system, was designed for streets “so steep as to make the use of horses difficult or impossible”. It used an “endless wire rope placed in a tube below the surface of the ground, between the tracks of a railroad”. A stationary engine kept the rope moving, while a gripping mechanism connected the moving rope to the cars above the street.The rope was contained in iron tubes and moved over sheaves along the route. A slot in the upper side of the tube allowed the gripping attachment from the car to reach the moving rope below the street. The grip could be engaged or released by the person operating the car, allowing the vehicle to move with the cable or stop when the rope was released. The source also states that the car could be started more smoothly than by horses and stopped on the road.How the 1873 Clay Street cable car covered a 5,197-foot steep inclineThe Cable Car Museum's reproduced description records that the Clay Street route began at the intersection of Kearny and Clay streets. The summit was 307 feet above Kearny Street, while the incline on Clay Street had double track and measured 5,197 feet in length. The source records a series of ascending and descending grades along the route, with the steepest grade listed as 1 in 6 15/100.The cable system itself used an endless steel wire rope three inches in circumference and 11,000 feet long. It was placed in iron tubes supported by sheaves, while an engine at the engine house drove the grip pulleys that moved the rope. The source states that the rope operated for 17½ hours a day at a speed of six miles per hour, with cars starting every five minutes except in the afternoon, when they started every three minutes.San Francisco’s cable car system expanded to 53 miles by 1883The Clay Street Hill Railroad was the only cable car company in San Francisco for four years. The Sutter Street Railroad developed its own version of Hallidie's patented system and began cable service in 1877. Other companies followed, in including the California Street Cable Railroad in 1878, the Geary Street, Park & Ocean Railroad in 1880, the Presidio & Ferries Railroad in 1882, the Market Street Cable Railway in 1883, the Ferries & Cliff House Railway in 1888 and the Omnibus Railroad & Cable Company in 1889. The museum states that San Francisco companies eventually laid 53 miles of track extending from the Ferry Building to the Presidio, Golden Gate Park, the Castro and the Mission.Electric streetcars later became the preferred form of city transit because they required only half the investment to build and maintain, could reach more areas and were quicker. However, cable cars remained capable of travelling over San Francisco's steep hills, and some lines were rebuilt. By 1947, the lower operating costs of buses led Mayor Lapham to call for the removal of the cable car lines. A public campaign led by Friedel Klussmann and the Citizens' Committee to Save the Cable Cars resulted in Measure 10, which passed and ordered the city to maintain the Powell Street cable car system.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2017, Chile certified Chañaral Island free of invasive rabbits; seven years later, rare seabirds had four active natural nests there with help from audio lures
articles.summary: In a significant conservation success, the Peruvian diving petrel is nesting naturally on Chañaral Island for the first time in over 40 years, seven years after invasive rabbits were removed. This article explores the efforts made to revive the seabird population and its implications for biodiversity.
articles.body: In early 2024, conservationists visiting Chañaral Island, off the coast of Chile, found four active natural nests of the Peruvian diving petrel, a small ground-nesting seabird that had stopped nesting on the island decades earlier. According to Island Conservation's release of 6 February 2024, the nests were the first active natural ones there in over four decades, and they appeared roughly six to seven years after the island was declared free of invasive rabbits. According to the announcement, the nests followed social attraction efforts that used solar-powered audio devices to play the petrel's call.Chañaral lost about 100,000 breeding pairs of Peruvian diving petrels to foxes and rabbitsChañaral was once home to the world’s largest colonies of Peruvian diving petrels, but in recent decades about 100,000 breeding pairs have been lost due to the introduction of foxes and rabbits. While the foxes ate the petrels, the rabbits made them flee from their nests by uprooting the vegetation in the surrounding areas. The foxes were eliminated some decades back, yet the rabbits survived and prevented the petrels from nesting.Rabbit removal on Choros from 2013 and Chañaral certified rabbit-free in late 2017The removal was led by Chile's National Forestry Corporation, known as CONAF, working with Island Conservation. The project began on Choros Island in 2013 and later expanded to the larger Chañaral Island. In 2014, rabbits were eradicated from Choros Island, and in 2017, certification of eradication was achieved on Chañaral Island.An experienced Labrador retriever named Finn contributed to confirming the eradication process of Choros. These two islands fall under the jurisdiction of the Humboldt Penguin National Reserve, which, together with other reserves on the coast of Atacama and Coquimbo, harbors nearly 80 percent of the world’s population of Humboldt penguins. The effects of the eradication process became evident on Choros Island very rapidly, where native seedlings were growing on hillsides and petrels settled in burrows previously used by rabbits.September 2019 social attraction project with two solar speakers and artificial burrowsClearing the land was just the beginning of the process. The implementation of the project for social attraction took place on Chañaral Island in September 2019 through collaboration between Island Conservation, CONAF, and Universidad Católica del Norte, together with technical assistance from Project Puffin. This strategy imitates both sight and sound that would be expected in a natural breeding colony. To do this, the team installed PVC artificial nests and two solar-powered speaker systems playing recordings of petrel calls. Park ranger Cristian Rivera said the petrels arrived within days of the speakers being installed. Motion-sensing cameras recorded regular visits. About a year and a half after installation, the team found its first naturally built burrows. After three years of work, it had found three such burrows and, using a burrowscope, documented the first chick seen on the island in 40 years. Island Conservation announced the chick in February 2023.Four active natural nests in early 2024, including two with chicks and one with a fledglingDuring a monitoring visit to Chañaral Island on 6 February 2024, Island Conservation and CONAF reported four active natural nests of Peruvian diving petrels: two with chicks, one with an adult, and one with a fledgling. According to Rivera, other sites that did not have the sound system exhibited no signs of the petrels, a sign that the speakers made all the difference. The International Union for Conservation of Nature had previously listed the species as endangered four years ago and has now listed it as near threatened, even though the species is still listed as endangered by the environment ministry of Chile. Coral Wolf of Island Conservation believes that the speakers will be removed someday because the birds will no longer require them.A 2020 study counted about 12,500 breeding pairs in Chile from 2010 to 2014, 95% of them on ChorosA peer-reviewed study published in 2020 in Bird Conservation International put the Chañaral story in context. Researchers surveyed Chile's colonies between 2010 and 2014 and found that the number of breeding pairs had increased to about 12,503, with a 95% confidence interval of 10,613 to 14,676. That was roughly 34% of the 36,450 pairs reported for Peru, and Choros Island held about 95% of Chile's total. The authors attributed the increase to legal protection of Choros, but they cautioned that this pattern alone could not justify a change in the species' conservation status, since time series were needed for all the other significant colonies. Because the survey data ended in 2014, before Chañaral was certified rabbit-free in 2017, the study could not show the effect of the eradication on Chañaral nests.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bid to delete 4.6k voters in 2 Karnataka assembly seats
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Complaints over attempts to mass-delete voter names from rolls surfaced in two Karnataka assembly constituencies during SIR, highlighting a
articles.body: BENGALURU: Complaints over attempts to mass-delete voter names from rolls surfaced in two Karnataka assembly constituencies during SIR, highlighting a discrepancy between EC's earlier claim of "nil" objections and data submitted during subsequent window to file claims and objections.Babaleshwar, represented by industries minister M B Patil, saw Form 7 applications seeking deletion of 1,682 names, while 2,928 names were sought to be deleted in Bhalki, constituency of rural development and panchayat raj minister Eshwar Khandre.A majority of those whose names were sought to be deleted belong to a minority community, while a sizeable number belongs to the Madar community among Dalits.Logical discrepancies: BLOs will collect docus from your homeHowever, most of these applications for mass deletion were withdrawn on Sept 23 over fear of triggering punitive measures if proven wrong.Vijayapura (Bijapur) district electoral officer and deputy commissioner Dr Anandh K, whose jurisdiction includes Babaleshwar, told TOI: “All mass applications for Form 7 were withdrawn in the district, except those filed by the family members themselves.”Data available on the CEO’s website shows between Sep 19 and 25, 131 persons in Bhalki had filed Form 7 applications covering 3,072 voters, while 40 persons in Babaleshwar sought deletion of 1,630 voters.Bidar DC Shilpa Sharma, who is also the DEO, told TOI those who raised objections were told to file the prescribed forms with affidavits and were also cautioned that they were liable to be punished if the information furnished by them was found to be incorrect.For voters who received notices because their names could not be mapped or because of “logical discrepancies”, the Election Commission’s revised guidelines announced Saturday offers some relief. BLOs will now visit their homes, collect supporting documents, and upload them for the ERO to decide. Such voters will not be typically called for a hearing.
